titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§144–145: The Pursuit of the Taichi'ud, and Jelme at the Qahan's Side
part: §§144–145 — The Flight of the Taichi'ud, and Jelme's Care of the Wounded Chinggis
about: Two sections. §144 is the great movement of the peoples after Jamuqa's defeat: the Naiman, Merkid, Oirat and Taichi'ud set out, Jamuqa plunders those who had raised a qan of their own, Wang Qan pursues him down the Ergune, and Chinggis pursues the Taichi'ud's A'uchu-Ba'atur to the Onon, where the two sides fight until nightfall and camp facing each other. §145 is the night after the battle: Chinggis, wounded in the neck vein, is kept alive by Jelme, who sucks out the clotted blood, strips and runs among the enemy for mare's milk, finds a vessel of curds, and gives it to him to drink; Chinggis wakes to a mire of blood, Jelme explains himself, and Chinggis declares what he owes him. The converb chains of §144 are broken at their natural pauses, and Jelme's plan to feign surrender (units from 'My heart naked going-when') rests heavily on the Ming glosses; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Naiman-u Buiruγ-Qān Altai-jin ebür Uluγ-Taγ žorin qaγačan ködölžüġüi.
sentences.l: Of-Naiman Buiruγ-Qān, Altai's bosom, Uluγ-Taγ pointing-at, parting, moving-is.
sentences.i: Buyiruq Qan of the Naiman, leaving the bosom of the Altai, was on the move toward Uluq-Taq.
sentences.n: The next five units share one frame: a people's name in the genitive, its leader, a place, then žorin 'pointing at' (converb -n) and ködölžüġüi. ködölžüġüi is ködöl- 'move' + the converb -žü + -ġüi, a contraction of bui 'is' (the Ming 動有 and 動了有 'moving-is, moved-is'); I render it 'was on the move'. Naiman-u is the genitive of the people, 'of the Naiman', placed before the leader's name (Ming 種(名)的). ebür is 'bosom, lap' (Ming 懷): the sheltered inner side of the range. Uluγ-Taγ is only 'place name' in the Ming; reading taγ as 'mountain' is my guess.

sentences.t: Merkid-ün Toγtoγ̇a-jin köġün Qutu Seleṅge žorin ködölžüġüi.
sentences.l: Of-Merkid Toγtoγ̇a-of son Qutu, Seleṅge pointing-at, moving-is.
sentences.i: Qutu, son of Toqto'a of the Merkid, was on the move toward the Selenge.
sentences.n: Same frame. Toγtoγ̇a-jin is the genitive -jin, the form used after a vowel (after a consonant it is -un/-ün). The order is 'of-Toqto'a son Qutu': possessor, noun, name in apposition (Ming 人名的 兒子 (兒)名). Seleṅge, the Ming says, is only a place name; I take it to be the river Selenge.

sentences.t: Oirad-un Quduγa-Beki Hoi temečen Šisgis žorin ködölžüġüi.
sentences.l: Of-Oirad Quduγa-Beki, Hoi (forest) struggling, Šisgis pointing-at, moving-is.
sentences.i: Quduqa-Beki of the Oirat, forcing his way through the forest, was on the move toward Shisgis.
sentences.n: Same frame, with one extra converb. Hoi is 'forest' (Ming 林) and temečen 爭 is 'striving, contending'; together I read 'struggling through the forest', but temeče- is inferred from the Ming alone and the pairing could be read otherwise. Shiratori prints Hoi with a capital, which might make it a name; the Ming gloss says forest. The Oirad are the Oirat, a forest people.

sentences.t: Taičiγ̇ud-un Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur Onan žorin ködölžüġüi.
sentences.l: Of-Taičiγ̇ud A'uchu-Hero, Onan pointing-at, moving-is.
sentences.i: A'uchu-Ba'atur of the Taichi'ud was on the move toward the Onon.
sentences.n: Same frame once more. Baγ̇atur is a title, 'hero', and sits inside the name (Ming 人名 勇士). The Taičiγ̇ud are written with a final -d, probably a plural, and take the genitive -un after it.

morph.gloss: the Taichi'ud, a clan (people name) [種(名)的]
genitive: of (back-vowel form, after a consonant)
A'uchu, a man's name [人名 勇士]

sentences.t: Žamuqa öġer(i)-jen qā ergügsed irgen-i daγ̇uliγ̇ad
sentences.l: Jamuqa own qā raised-ones people (acc.) plundering,
sentences.i: Jamuqa plundered the people who had raised a qan of their own,
sentences.n: The grammar of öġer(i)-jen qā ergügsed irgen-i is hard, and this unit rests on the Ming glosses. -jen is the reflexive-possessive 'one's own' (Ming 自的行), here on öġer; ergügsed is a participle with plural -d, 'those who have raised' (Ming 擡了的每); irgen-i is 'the people (object)'. So: 'the people who had raised their own qan'. Who they are, and whether 'own' belongs to the people or to Jamuqa, is not settled by the text. qā is qaγan in short form. Plundering (daγ̇uli-, from the Ming 搶) is a converb, and the sentence goes on in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
own, self (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel) [(自己)自(的行)]
qan, ruler (short form of qaγan; the long vowel as printed) [皇帝]
to lift, raise up, set up [擡了的每]
past participle with plural -d: those who have ...-ed
to plunder, seize (stem inferred; Ming 搶) [搶了]

sentences.t: Ergüne huruγ̇u Žamuqa qarin ködölžüġüi.
sentences.l: Ergüne down-along, Jamuqa back-turning, moving-is.
sentences.i: and Jamuqa turned back down the Ergune.
sentences.n: Continues the sentence of the unit above: the chain is plundering, then 'moved back'. huruγ̇u 'along, down along' (Ming 順着) is the word for following a river; I take 'down' from the sense of turning back. qarin is the converb of qari- 'return'.

morph.gloss: the Ergüne, a river (river name) [河名]
along, down along (postposition: "following" the river) [順着]
Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
is, was (contracted from bui, Ming 有)

sentences.t: An-i tein butalaγdažu Waṅ-Qān Ergüne huruγ̇u Žamuqa-ji nekebe.
sentences.l: Them (acc.) so scattering-being, Waṅ-Qān Ergüne down-along Jamuqa (acc.) pursued.
sentences.i: They being thus scattered, Wang Qan pursued Jamuqa down the Ergune.
sentences.n: An-i is 'them' (Ming 他每行), the accusative of the third-person plural, and butalaγdažu is the converb of a passive: 'being scattered' (butala-, 'scatter', is inferred from the Ming 潰散着). Whether 'them' means Jamuqa's following or the people he had just plundered is not clear to me. The sentence closes with nekebe, 'pursued', and the full stop. -ji on Žamuqa is the accusative after a vowel.

morph.gloss: them, those (oblique stem of the third-person plural; Ming 他每) [他每行]

the Ergüne, a river (river name) [河名]
along, down along (postposition: "following" the river) [順水]
Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to pursue (stem inferred; Ming 追襲) [追襲了]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Onan žüg Taičiγ̇ud-un Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur-i nekebe.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan Onan direction Taičiγ̇ud-of A'uchu-Hero (acc.) pursued.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan pursued A'uchu-Ba'atur of the Taichi'ud toward the Onon.
sentences.n: A parallel to the sentence before: the same verb nekebe, with Chinggis as subject. žüg is 'side, direction' (Ming 處) and stands after Onan, 'toward the Onon'. The accusative -i is on the whole name Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur-i.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)名]

sentences.t: Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur ulus-tur(i)-jan kürüġed ulus(i)-jan dürbeġülün ködölgeġed
sentences.l: A'uchu-Hero people-to-own reaching, people-own hurrying-causing, setting-in-motion-having.
sentences.i: Reaching his own people, A'uchu-Ba'atur hurried them and set them moving.
sentences.n: The first part of a converb chain that runs on for several units; I have broken it at the first natural pause. ulus-tur(i)-jan is ulus 'people' + dative-locative -tur + the reflexive-possessive -jan 'his own' (Ming 百姓裏自的行): 'to his own people'. dürbeġülün is dürbe- 'hurry' + causative -ġül- + -n: 'making hurry'. ködölgeġed is ködöl- 'move' + causative -ge-: 'having set in motion'. The brackets (i) are Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: A'uchu, a man's name [人名 勇士]
people, realm [百姓 裏自的行]

to hurry (stem inferred; Ming 忙走) [忙走]

sentences.t: Aγ̇uču-Baγ̇atur Qotun-Orčaṅ Taičiγ̇ud Onan-u činaži edeġed hüleġüd
sentences.l: A'uchu-Hero, Qotun-Orčaṅ, the Taičiγ̇ud, Onan-of that-side, one-side the-rest,
sentences.i: A'uchu-Ba'atur, Qotun-Orchang and the Taichi'ud, on the far side of the Onon, some and the rest,
sentences.n: The subject of the next unit: the two leaders and their clan, set out on 'that side of the Onon' (činaži, Ming 那廂). The pair edeġed hüleġüd (Ming 一邊 and 多餘, 'one side' and 'the remainder') I can only render as 'some, and the rest'; the stems are unknown to me and the Ming glosses are all I have. I split here because the sentence has no punctuation until baižuγ̇ui and runs fourteen words.

morph.gloss: A'uchu, a man's name [人名 勇士]
Qotun-Orchang, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
the Taichi'ud, a clan (people name; the -d is plural) [種(名)每]
that side, yonder (adverb; the ending -ži is not clear) [那廂]
one side, this part (stem uncertain; Ming 一邊) [一邊]
the rest, the remainder (stem uncertain; Ming 多餘) [多餘]

sentences.t: tulastan čeriġüd(i)-jen žasažu qadqulduja keġen žasažu baižuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Shield-having troops-own arranging, 'let-us-fight' saying, arranging, standing-is.
sentences.i: arranged their shielded troops, saying "Let us fight," and stood in order of battle.
sentences.n: The predicate of the unit above. tulastan is tulas (Ming 方牌, 'square tablet', shield) + the plural possessive -tan: 'shield-having ones'; čeriġüd(i)-jen is 'their own troops'. žasažu 'preparing' is said twice, once before and once after the quoted purpose; qadqulduja keġen is a hortative -ja 'let us' followed by keġen 'saying', the Ming 麼道 that opens or closes a quotation. Shiratori marks no quotation marks here. baižuγ̇ui is bai- 'stand' + -žu + -γ̇ui (bui 'is').

morph.gloss: square shield (Ming 方牌, "square tablet"; uncertain) [方牌 有的每]
plural (the linking ü and the (i) are Shiratori's)
to prepare, set in order [整治着]
to fight, strike (stem inferred from the Ming 殺) [厮殺︀咱]
to prepare, set in order [整治着]
to stand, be placed (Ming 立) [立着有]
is, was (contracted from bui, Ming 有)

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan kürüġed Taičiγ̇ud-luγ̇a qadqulduba.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan reaching, Taičiγ̇ud-with fought.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan came up and fought the Taichi'ud.
sentences.n: kürüġed is the converb 'having reached' (kür- + -üġed). -luγ̇a is the comitative 'with' (Ming 和他). The reciprocal -ldu- on qadqulduba means 'one another', which is how Mongol says 'fought with'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)名]

sentences.t: Maši egerün egerün qadquldužu žilda boldažu
sentences.l: Very turning-over turning-over fighting, late becoming,
sentences.i: Fighting hard, back and forth, until it grew late,
sentences.n: Maši 'very' (Ming 好生) with the doubled egerün (Ming 翻覆 twice) gives 'turning over and over', that is, the line swayed back and forth. egerün is a converb with a linking vowel. boldažu is bol- 'become' + an element -da- + -žu; the Ming 被做着 suggests a passive 'being made', but I only know it means 'it growing late' here. Converb chain, broken after boldažu.

morph.gloss: to turn over, reverse (stem inferred; Ming 翻覆) [翻覆]
to turn over, reverse (stem inferred; Ming 翻覆) [翻覆]
stem-extender (the Ming 被 hints at a passive; uncertain)

sentences.t: mün qadqulduγsan γažar-a situldužu qonoba.
sentences.l: Just fought-place-at facing-off, spent-the-night.
sentences.i: they camped facing one another on the very ground where they had fought.
sentences.n: mün is the emphatic 'just, the very' (Ming 只). qadqulduγsan is a participle, 'that which was fought', used before γažar 'place'; -a is the dative-locative (Ming 地行). situldužu is the reciprocal of a stem situ- (inferred from the Ming 相抗着, 'facing off, withstanding'). qonoba is 'lodged for the night'. End of the Taichi'ud engagement for the day.

morph.gloss: to oppose, face off (stem inferred; Ming 相抗) [相抗着]
to spend the night, lodge [宿了]

sentences.t: Ulus ba dürbežü aisurun
sentences.l: People also hurrying, coming-when,
sentences.i: As the people, too, came hurrying in,
sentences.n: ba after the noun is 'also' (Ming 也), the same word that elsewhere means 'and'; Ulus here is 'the people' (Ming 百姓每). aisurun is a time converb in -run, 'when coming'; the stem aisu- is inferred from the Ming 來時. Broken from the next unit, which carries the main verb.

morph.gloss: people, realm (here "the people", Ming 百姓每) [百姓每]
also, and (particle; Ming 也, 并) [也]
to hurry, to flee in haste (stem inferred) [忙起着]
to come, draw near (stem inferred; Ming 來) [來時]

sentences.t: mün-kü tende čeriγ̇üd-lüġe-ben qamtu küreġeležü qonolduba.
sentences.l: Just-there troops-with-own together ring-camping, lodged-together.
sentences.i: they made a ring camp together with their own troops, and passed the night there.
sentences.n: mün-kü is 'just, indeed' (Ming 也), here 'right there'. -lüġe is the comitative (Ming 一處/自的行): 'with their own troops'. küreġeležü is the converb of küreġele- 'to camp in a ring' (Ming 札營着), the circular camp of the steppe; qonolduba is 'lodged together'. The subject is the people of the previous unit, not Chinggis, so I have written 'they'.

morph.gloss: to camp in a ring, make a circle camp (Ming 札營) [札營着]
to spend the night, lodge [共宿了]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan tere qadqulduγ̇an-dur sužijasu-ban šilür- težü
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan that fight-in neck-vein-own wounded-being,
sentences.i: In that battle Chinggis Qahan was wounded in the neck vein,
sentences.n: §145 opens with the story of the wound and Jelme's care. sužijasu-ban is 'the vein of the neck' (Ming 項頸脉) + -ban, 'his own' (the reflexive-possessive), so 'his own neck vein', which the English turns into 'his'. qadqulduγ̇an-dur is 'in the fighting': the ending -γ̇an makes a noun from the reciprocal stem, and the Ming 陣 reads it as the battle line. The verb is split across the line: šilür-težü, Ming 被傷着, 'being wounded'. I do not know what the -te- is; the Ming 被 hints at a passive. This is the first of several converbs.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
the vein of the neck (Ming 項頸脉) [項頸脉 自的(行)]
to be wounded (stem inferred; Ming 被傷; the word runs on to težü across the line) [被傷]
ending of the stem (the Ming 被 suggests a passive; uncertain) [着]

sentences.t: čisun töridgeġešü ülü bolun amduriγdarun
sentences.l: Blood if-made-to-stop not ceasing, being-flustered-when,
sentences.i: and the blood would not stop though they tried to stanch it. In the alarm,
sentences.n: töridgeġešü is a stem töri- 'stop' (inferred from the Ming 止) + the causative -dge- (Ming 敎) + the conditional -ġešü (Shiratori writes š for the usual s): 'if one makes it stop'. ülü bolun is 'not ceasing' (Ming 不 住). ülü is the negative used with converbs and the present; ese is kept for plain past events. amduriγdarun is a passive stem + the time converb -run: 'when flustered', Ming 被荒忙時. Who is flustered is not stated: the attendants, surely, but I have left it open.

morph.gloss: to stop, stanch (stem inferred; Ming 止) [敎止呵]
to become; here "to cease, stop" (Ming 住) [住]
to be flustered, alarmed (stem inferred; Ming 荒忙) [被荒忙 時]

sentences.t: naran šingeġülün mün tende situldužu baγ̇užu
sentences.l: Sun sinking, just-there facing-off, camping,
sentences.i: and the sun sank, the armies halted and stood off from one another there.
sentences.n: naran 'sun' (Ming 日) and šingeġülün (Ming 落後, 'fall behind') give 'the sun going down'; I have no stem šingeġül- and the reading rests on the Ming. situldužu again 'facing off' and baγ̇užu 'came down, halted' (Ming 下着). The subject of the last two converbs is the armies, not Jelme; Shiratori's text does not give it.

morph.gloss: to sink, set (stem inferred; Ming 落後, "fall behind") [落後]
to oppose, face off (stem inferred; Ming 相抗) [相抗拒着]
to come down, halt for the night (Ming 下) [下着]

sentences.t: böglegsen čisun-i Želme šimin šimin ama-γ̇an čisudažu
sentences.l: Clotted blood (acc.) Jelme sucking, sucking, mouth-own blood-stained,
sentences.i: Jelme sucked at the clotted blood, again and again, until his own mouth was stained,
sentences.n: böglegsen is a participle, 'that which has clotted', from bögle- 'to plug, clog' (Ming 塞了的); čisun-i is the accusative, 'blood as object'. šimin is a converb, said twice (Ming 咂着 twice): 'sucking and sucking'. ama-γ̇an is ama 'mouth' + -γ̇an, the reflexive-possessive after a vowel. čisudažu is 'blood-stained' (Ming 被血汚着). Note that the blood is the wound's, not that of the enemy.

morph.gloss: to clog, stop up, clot (stem inferred; Ming 塞) [塞了的]
Jelme, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to be stained with blood (stem inferred from čisun; Ming 被血汚) [被血汚着]

sentences.t: Želme busu küġün ülü itegen sakildužu saγ̇užu süni düli boltala
sentences.l: Jelme other man not relying, guarding, sitting, night's middle until,
sentences.i: Jelme, trusting no one else, kept watch and sat there until the middle of the night,
sentences.n: busu 'other' (Ming 別) with küġün 'man' and ülü itegen 'not trusting' (Ming 不 倚附) gives 'trusting no other person'. itegen is likely a converb of ite- 'rely on' but I only know it from the Ming. sakildužu is the reciprocal converb of sakil- 'guard' (Ming 相守着). boltala is the converb in -tala, 'until it became', here 'until': süni düli boltala 'until night became half'.

morph.gloss: Jelme, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
relying on, trusting (probably ite- + converb -gen; Ming 倚附; uncertain) [倚附]
to guard, keep watch (stem inferred; Ming 守) [相守着]

sentences.t: böglegsen čisun-i ama-γ̇ar düġüreṅ žalkiγ̇ad asqaγ̇ad
sentences.l: Clotted blood (acc.) mouth-with full, swallowing, spitting-out,
sentences.i: filling his mouth with the clotted blood, he swallowed it and spat it out,
sentences.n: Another converb chain. ama-γ̇ar is the instrumental of ama, 'with the mouth' (Ming 敎口, the Ming's 敎 meaning 'causing the mouth to …'), and düġüreṅ is 'to the full' (Ming 滿). žalkiγ̇ad 'swallowing' and asqaγ̇ad 'spitting' (Ming 嚥 and 吐) are two converbs in -γ̇ad. The blood was drawn from the wound; that he swallowed some is the point of the Qahan's later speech.

morph.gloss: to clog, stop up, clot (stem inferred; Ming 塞) [塞了的]
full, to the full (adverb; Ming 滿) [滿]
to spit out, vomit, cast away (Ming 吐) [吐了]

sentences.t: süni düli nögčiġešü Čiṅgis Qaγan dotora-γ̇an sergüžü ügülerün:
sentences.l: Night middle when-passed, Čiṅgis Qaγan inside-own awakening, saying:
sentences.i: When midnight had passed, Chinggis Qahan came to himself and said:
sentences.n: nögčiġešü is a conditional with š as before; the stem nögči- 'pass' is inferred from the Ming 過. dotora-γ̇an is 'inside, within' + reflexive -γ̇an (Ming 內自的行): the Ming makes it 'from his own inside', which I take as 'he came to himself'. sergüžü is 'waking' and ügülerün the time converb 'saying' that introduces a speech.

morph.gloss: to pass, go by (stem inferred; Ming 過) [過呵]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.t: "Čisun qaγču baraba. Undaγ̇asumu bi" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Blood dried finished. Thirsty-am I," said.
sentences.i: "The blood has dried up. I am thirsty," he said.
sentences.n: Shiratori opens a quotation at Čisun. qaγču is 'dry' (Ming 乾着); baraba is bara- 'finish' + past, 'has come to an end'. Undaγ̇asumu (Ming 渴有) is 'is thirsty': I treat undaγ̇a- as 'thirst' and -su- as an extender, but the stem is a guess. The verb of speech keġebe comes after the bracket.

morph.gloss: dry, having dried (converb; stem uncertain; Ming 乾着) [乾]
to be finished, used up (Ming 着了) [着了]
to be thirsty (stem inferred; Ming 渴) [渴有]

sentences.t: Tendēče Želme maqalai γudusun deġel-qubčasun(i)-jan bügüde-ji talžu
sentences.l: Thence Jelme cap boots robe-clothes-own all (acc.) taking-off,
sentences.i: Thereupon Jelme took off his cap, his boots and all his clothes,
sentences.n: Tendēče is tende 'there' + the ablative -ēče (Ming 自那裏): 'from there', which as a narrative joint means 'thereupon'. deġel-qubčasun(i)-jan is a compound 'robe-clothing' with the reflexive-possessive -jan (Ming 衣服 自的行); bügüde-ji 'all' takes the accusative. talžu is 'stripping off' (Ming 脫着); I do not know the stem, so I have read tal- from the Ming alone.

morph.gloss: Jelme, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
robe, outer garment [衣服 自的行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to strip off, take off (stem inferred; Ming 脫) [脫着]

sentences.t: γaγča dotoγ̇aži- tu čurama-ničügün situldužu baiqun dain dotoraγ̇un güjižü
sentences.l: Only drawers-having stark-naked, facing-off standing enemy inside, running,
sentences.i: and, wearing only his drawers and otherwise bare, ran into the midst of the enemy who stood opposed,
sentences.n: A hard unit. γaγča is 'only' (Ming 獨), dotoγ̇aži-tu is split over a line: dotoγ̇aži 'drawers' (Ming 袴) + -tu, the possessive 'having' (Ming 有的), 'drawers-having'. čurama-ničügün is Ming 赤裸 'bare', čurama perhaps an intensifier. situldužu baiqun is 'standing facing off', with dain 'enemy'; dotoraγ̇un (Ming 裏面) 'into the inside'. Whether the enemy are the subject of baiqun, or Jelme, is open. güjižü is 'rushing' (Ming 走着).

morph.gloss: drawers, trousers (Ming 袴; first half of a word split at the line end) [袴]
possessive: having ... (Ming 有的; second half of dotoγ̇aži-tu) [有的]
stark naked (Ming 赤裸; čurama perhaps an intensifier; uncertain) [赤裸]
to oppose, face off (stem inferred; Ming 相抗) [相抗拒着]
participle ending (Ming 立着; form uncertain)
inside, into the midst (Ming 裏面; dotora + a direction ending, uncertain) [裏面]
to run, rush (stem inferred; Ming 走) [走着]

sentences.t: činana kürelegsen irgen-ü tergen-dür an-u unužu esüġüd erižü jadažu
sentences.l: That-side camped people's cart-on his mounting, mare's-milks seeking, unable,
sentences.i: He climbed onto a cart of the people camped on the far side and hunted for mare's milk, and could not find it,
sentences.n: činana is 'on that side' (Ming 那邊), kürelegsen 'those who had camped in a ring' (Ming (下)營了的), irgen-ü is 'of the people', with -ü, the front-vowel genitive. tergen-dür is 'on the cart'. an-u, Ming 他的 'his, their', stands before the converb unužu 'mounting'. esüġüd is the plural of esüg 'mare's milk'. erižü jadažu is a converb pair: 'seeking, not being able'. jadažu (Ming 不能着) acts as 'could not'; the 'could not find' is mine.

morph.gloss: to camp in a ring (compare küreġeležü; Ming (下)營) [(下)營了的]
his, their (third-person genitive stem, back-vowel counterpart of in-) [他的]
to be unable (Ming 不能) [不能着]

sentences.t: dürberün geġüd(i)-jen ülü saγ̇an talbiγsad ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Hurrying-when, mares-own not milked, left-ones had.
sentences.i: In the haste of flight they had left their mares unmilked.
sentences.n: dürberün is the time converb 'when hurrying' (Ming 因忙走時); the subject changes here to the people of the camp, who had fled. geġüd(i)-jen is 'their own mares' (Ming 騍馬(每)自的行), the (i) being Shiratori's. ülü saγ̇an talbiγsad is 'not milking, having left'. ažuγ̇u (Ming 有來) is the past 'had'. This explains why there was no milk.

morph.gloss: to hurry, flee in haste [因忙走時]
mare (stem uncertain; Ming 騍馬) [騍馬(每)自的行]
to set down, leave, let go [放了]
to be, to have been [有來]
past: used to be, had (Ming 有來)

sentences.t: Esüg olun jadažu
sentences.l: Mare's-milk finding unable,
sentences.i: Unable to get any mare's milk,
sentences.n: Esüg is 'mare's milk' again, with olun 'getting' (Ming 得) and jadažu 'being unable'. Short, but it is the hinge of the sentence: the next unit says what he took instead.

morph.gloss: to be unable (Ming 不能) [不能着]

sentences.t: nigen jeke büriġetei taraγ tergen-eče in-ü abuγ̇ad ergüžü irebe.
sentences.l: One big vessel-having curds cart-from his taking, lifting, came.
sentences.i: he took from their cart a big vessel of curds, lifted it, and came back with it.
sentences.n: büriġetei is büriġe 'vessel' (stem inferred from the Ming 器皿盛來的) + the possessive -tei, 'vessel-having', so 'a big vessel-having curds'; I read it as 'a big vessel of curds'. tergen-eče is the ablative 'from the cart' (Ming 車處) and in-ü is the genitive 'his' (Ming 他的). abuγ̇ad ergüžü irebe is a chain: 'taking, lifting, came'. taraγ is curds, sour milk (Ming 酪).

morph.gloss: vessel, container (stem inferred; Ming 器皿) [器︀中盫來的]

sentences.t: Žaγ̇ura odorun ba irerün ba küġün-(n)e ese üžegdebe.
sentences.l: Meanwhile going-when and coming-when and by-people not seen.
sentences.i: In all that time, going and coming, no one saw him.
sentences.n: Here ese 'not' (Ming 不曾), the negative of a past action, meets a passive: üžegdebe is üže- 'see' + -gde- 'be …-ed' + past: 'was not seen'. küġün-(n)e is the dative-locative used as the agent, 'by people' (Ming 被人行); the (n) is Shiratori's. odorun and irerün are time converbs, 'when going' and 'when coming', each followed by ba 'and' (Ming 并).

morph.gloss: also, and (particle; Ming 也, 并) [幷]
also, and (particle; Ming 也, 并) [幷]
dative-locative, here the agent after a passive: by (the bracketed n is Shiratori's)

sentences.t: Teṅgeri kü igeġebe že.
sentences.l: Heaven indeed protected, indeed.
sentences.i: Heaven itself protected him.
sentences.n: kü is the emphatic particle (Ming 只), putting weight on Teṅgeri 'Heaven'. igeġebe 'protected, helped' (Ming 護助了) is from a stem I know only from the Ming. že is the Ming 也者, a particle of assent, 'so'.

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power [天]
to protect, help (stem inferred; Ming 護助) [護助了]

sentences.t: Taraγ büriġetü-ji abčiraγ̇ad
sentences.l: Curds vessel-having (acc.) bringing,
sentences.i: Bringing the vessel of curds,
sentences.n: büriġetü-ji is the same büriġe + -tü 'having', with the accusative -ji after the vowel: 'the vessel-having thing'. abčiraγ̇ad is 'having brought' (Ming 將來了): perhaps abču + ire- 'taking, come'. Continues in the next unit.

morph.gloss: vessel, container [器︀中盫來有的 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to bring, fetch (abču "taking" + ire- "come", Ming 將來) [將來了]

sentences.t: mün Želme öġesün kü usun erižü abčiražü taraγ žiġürežü Qaγ̇an-a üγ̇ulba.
sentences.l: Just Jelme self indeed water seeking bringing curds mixing, Qaγan-to made-drink.
sentences.i: Jelme himself found water, brought it, mixed it with the curds, and gave it to the Qahan to drink.
sentences.n: öġesün (Ming 自己) is 'himself' and kü adds 'indeed' (Ming 只): the point is that Jelme did it with his own hands. erižü abčiražü žiġürežü is a three-step chain: 'seeking, bringing, mixing' (Ming 尋着 要着 調着). žiġüre- 'mix, dilute' is from the Ming 調 and not from any word I know. Qaγ̇an-a is the dative 'to the Qahan' (Ming 行). üγ̇ulba is ü- 'drink' + causative -γ̇ul- + past, 'made drink'.

morph.gloss: Jelme, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
oneself, one's own (Ming 自己; form uncertain) [自己]
to mix, temper (stem inferred; Ming 調) [調着]

sentences.t: γurbanta amužu üžu Qaγan ügü- lerün:
sentences.l: Three-times resting drinking, Qaγan saying:
sentences.i: Three times he rested and drank, and the Qahan said:
sentences.n: γurbanta 'three times' (Ming 三次) with amužu 'resting' and üžu 'drinking' (ü- 'drink' + -žu; Ming 飮着). The speech verb is split over the line: ügü- | lerün, which I treat as ügüle- + the time converb -rün.

morph.gloss: to rest, pause (Ming 歇息) [歇息着]
to speak (first half of ügü-lerün, split at the line end) [說]
verb-maker (second half of the split word) []

sentences.t: "Dotora nidün min-u geibe" keġeġed
sentences.l: "Inside my eyes cleared," saying-having,
sentences.i: "My eyes have cleared," he said,
sentences.n: Shiratori opens the quotation at Dotora. dotora 'inside' (Ming 內行) is a locative noun, 'within'. nidün min-u is 'eye of mine' (Ming 眼 我的): the possessor before the noun. geibe is gei- 'become light' + past: 'has grown light'. keġeġed is the converb 'having said'.

morph.gloss: inside, within (here "in me", Ming 內行) [內行]
to grow light, clear (Ming 明) [明了]

sentences.t: öndeižü saγ̇utala üdür geižü gegen bolžu
sentences.l: Stretching-sitting-up, sitting-while day dawning light becoming,
sentences.i: Stretching, he sat up, and while he sat day dawned and it grew light,
sentences.n: öndeižü 'stretching, rising' (Ming 欠伸起着) is a converb, then saγ̇utala 'while sitting' (-tala 'while, until'); geižü 'dawning' and bolžu 'becoming' are two more converbs in the chain. üdür is 'day' (Ming 日).

morph.gloss: to stretch oneself, sit up (stem inferred; Ming 欠伸起) [欠伸起着]

sentences.t: üžeġesü tere saγ̇uγsan horčin
sentences.l: Looked-when that sat-place around,
sentences.i: When he looked, around the place where he had been sitting
sentences.n: üžeġesü is the conditional 'when he looked'; saγ̇uγsan is a participle, 'that which was sat', and tere saγ̇uγsan horčin 'around that sitting-place' (Ming 周圍). The sentence goes on in the next unit.

morph.gloss: surroundings, round about (Ming 周圍) [周圍]

sentences.t: Želme-jin šimin šimin böglegsen čisun asqaγsan horčin namurγan bolžuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Jelme-of sucking sucking clotted blood spat-out around, mire becoming-was.
sentences.i: and around Jelme, where he had sucked and spat out the clotted blood, the ground had become a mire.
sentences.n: Želme-jin is the genitive 'of Jelme'; it stands before the whole participle phrase, which is the relative clause 'the clotted blood he sucked, sucked and spat'. horčin 'around' recurs. namurγan is 'mire, mud' (Ming 陷泥); the exact form is from the Ming. bolžuγ̇u is 'had become' (Ming 做了有).

morph.gloss: to clog, stop up, clot (stem inferred; Ming 塞) [塞了的]
surroundings, round about (Ming 周圍) [周圍]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan üžežü ügülerün:
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan seeing, saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan saw it and said:
sentences.n: A routine frame: subject, converb of seeing (üže-), time converb of speaking (ügülerün). The quotation follows in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.t: "Ene jaγ̇un bolumu; qolo asqaγ̇asu ambar ažuγ̇u" keġebe.
sentences.l: "This what has-been-made? Far having-cast-away how would-it-have-been?" said.
sentences.i: "What is this? Why not have spat it far away?" he said.
sentences.n: A two-part question. Ene jaγ̇un bolumu is 'this, what is it/done?' (Ming 這 甚 做有); the semicolon is Shiratori's. qolo asqaγ̇asu ambar ažuγ̇u is 'far, if you had cast it, how would it have been?': a conditional -γ̇asu + ambar 'how' (Ming 怎生) + ažuγ̇u 'would be' (Ming 有來); the implied sense is 'why not spit it further off'. asqa- has meant 'spit' above (Ming 吐); here the Ming reads 棄 'cast away'.

morph.gloss: to spit out, cast away [棄呵]
to be, to have been [有(來)]
past: used to be, had (Ming 有來)

sentences.t: Tendēče Želme ügülerün:
sentences.l: Thence Jelme saying:
sentences.i: Then Jelme said:
sentences.n: Tendēče 'from there' as above, Želme named, ügülerün 'saying'. The speech follows.

morph.gloss: Jelme, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: "Čima-ji amduriγdarun qolo oduγ̇asu čima-dāča alžijaqui-ača ajužu
sentences.l: "You (acc.) flustered-when far if-I-went, you-from separated-from fearing,
sentences.i: "When you were in distress, I could not go far; I feared being parted from you,
sentences.n: A stack of case endings. čima-ji, Ming 你行, is the accusative of či 'you', formed on the oblique stem čima-; čima-dāča is the ablative 'from you' (Ming 你處) with the long vowel as Shiratori prints it. oduγ̇asu is the conditional 'if I went'. alžijaqui-ača is a participle + ablative, 'from being apart' (Ming 離了的行): the stem is inferred. ajužu is 'fearing'. The sentence has no verb until much later and the translation joins it to the next unit.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to be flustered, alarmed (stem inferred; Ming 荒忙) [被荒忙 時]
to be apart, separated (stem inferred; Ming 離) [離了的行]
to fear, be afraid (Ming 怕) [怕著︀]

sentences.t: jaγ̇aražu žalkiqu-ji žalkiγ̇ad žasqaqu-ji asqaγ̇ad andurižu
sentences.l: hurrying, to-swallow-what (acc.) swallowing, to-spit-what (acc.) spitting, flustered,
sentences.i: and in my haste, in my confusion, I swallowed what I should have swallowed and spat out what I should have spat,
sentences.n: Mongol participles with the accusative: žalkiqu-ji 'what is to be swallowed' and žasqaqu-ji 'what is to be spat'; the Ming gives 嚥的行 and 吐的行. Shiratori prints the second with a stray initial ž, žasqaqu for asqaqu; I take it as a misprint copied from the word before. jaγ̇aražu, andurižu are converbs 'hurrying' and 'flustered'.

morph.gloss: to hurry (stem inferred; Ming 忙) [忙着]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to spit out (printed with a stray initial ž) [吐的行]
to spit out, vomit, cast away (Ming 吐) [吐了]
to be flustered (compare amduri-; Ming 荒) [荒着]

sentences.t: keġeli-dür min-u teki kedüi oroba." keġebe.
sentences.l: in-belly my also some entered," said.
sentences.i: and some of it went into my belly too."
sentences.n: keġeli-dür 'in the belly' (Ming 肚 裏) and min-u 'my'; teki 'also, even' (Ming 也); kedüi 'some, a little' (Ming 幾些). oroba is 'entered' and the closing quote is on oroba. keġebe 'said' is outside the quotation. Jelme is admitting that he swallowed some of the Qahan's blood.

morph.gloss: some, a little, how much (Ming 幾些) [幾些]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan basa ügülerün:
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan again saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan spoke again:
sentences.n: basa 'again' (Ming 再) with the usual speaking frame.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.t: "Nama-ji eimü bolžu kebten böġetele ničügün jakin güjižü oroba či.
sentences.l: "Me (acc.) thus becoming lying while, naked why running entered you.
sentences.i: "While I lay here like this, why did you run in naked?
sentences.n: Nama-ji is 'me' (Ming 我行), the accusative on the oblique stem nama-. eimü bolžu 'thus becoming' (Ming 這般 做着), kebten 'lying down' (Ming 臥), and böġetele, the time converb of bü- 'to be' with the Ming 有間, 'while being'. ničügün 'naked' (Ming 赤裸). jakin is 'why' (Ming 爲甚).

morph.gloss: me (oblique stem of bi "I") [我 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to run, rush (stem inferred; Ming 走) [走着]

sentences.t: Bariγdaγ̇asu nama-ji eimü-ji ülü-ü žiγ̇aqu büleġe či keġebe.
sentences.l: If-seized me (acc.) thus (acc.) not-? to-tell was you, said.
sentences.i: If you had been seized, would you not have told them of me like this?" he said.
sentences.n: A difficult sentence, and my reading is the least sure here. bariγdaγ̇asu is the passive conditional, 'if seized'. nama-ji eimü-ji: both take the accusative -ji and the Ming has 行 on both, so it is 'me, in this way'. ülü-ü is ülü 'not' with the question particle -ü (Ming 不…麽); žiγ̇aqu büleġe is 'would have told' (Ming 吿麽 有來). I take it that Chinggis scolds Jelme for risking capture: a prisoner would be made to speak. The quotation has no closing quotation mark.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
thus, in this way [這般 行]
accusative (Ming 行; the function here is not clear)
question particle (Ming 麽 on the next word)
to tell, report (stem inferred; Ming 吿) [吿麽]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: Želme ügülerün:
sentences.l: Jelme saying:
sentences.i: Jelme said:
sentences.n: Standard frame.

morph.gloss: Jelme, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.t: "Min-u sedkil ničügün odorun ker-ber bariγdaγ̇asu bi tan-dur oroqu duratu büleġe.
sentences.l: "My heart naked going-when if seized, I you-to enter-intending was.
sentences.i: "My thought was this: if I were seized going naked, I would go over to you.
sentences.n: The speech opens: min-u sedkil is 'my heart, my intent' (Ming 我的 心). ker-ber is 'if' (Ming 若是); odorun 'when going'; bariγdaγ̇asu 'if seized'. tan-dur is the plural 'you' with the dative-locative: 'to you'. This 'you' is, I think, the enemy that he would pretend to join; oroqu duratu is 'entering will-having' (Ming 投的 心 有的), 'meaning to go over (surrender)'. The next units give the rest of his plan, as he told it.

morph.gloss: you (plural; oblique stem of ta) [您行]
to enter, go over to (Ming 投) [投的]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: uqažu barižu alaja keġen
sentences.l: Perceiving, seizing, 'let-us-kill' saying,
sentences.i: If they noticed me, seized me and said "Let us kill him,"
sentences.n: uqažu 'perceiving' and barižu 'seizing' are converbs, alaja is the hortative 'let us kill', followed by keġen 'saying' (Ming 麼道). The subject, the enemy, is not named; the clause is a supposed event. Shiratori gives no break.

sentences.t: qubčasun min-u bügüde-ji talžu γaγča emüdün taluγ̇a üdüġüj-e mültüš aldaγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: Clothes my all (acc.) taking-off, only trousers strip, not-yet suddenly causing-to-slip,
sentences.i: I would strip off all my clothes, leaving only my trousers, and, before they were ready, suddenly slip away from them,
sentences.n: The least certain unit. qubčasun min-u bügüde-ji talžu is 'taking off all my clothes' (Ming 脫着). γaγča emüdün taluγ̇a, Ming 獨 袴 脫, would be 'only the trousers (to) strip', which I cannot reconcile with 'taking off all my clothes' unless it means 'strip, leaving only my trousers'. The ending -γ̇a on taluγ̇a is not explained. üdüġüj-e (Ming 未 行) 'not yet' and mültüš 'suddenly' (Ming 倐然), with aldaγ̇ulžu 'causing to slip/lose' (Ming 敎脫了着): the plan is to leave the clothes in their hands and escape.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to strip off, take off (stem inferred; Ming 脫) [脫着]
not yet, before (Ming 未) [未 行]
dative-locative: at (the j is a linking sound; uncertain)
to lose, let slip [敎脫了着]

sentences.t: tan-dur edüi idürežü irebe bi keġekü büleġe.
sentences.l: You-to this-much hastening came I saying was.
sentences.i: and I would say to you: 'I have hurried this far to come to you.'
sentences.n: tan-dur 'to you' as before (Ming 您行); edüi 'this much' (Ming 這些); idürežü 'hastening' (Ming 趕到着), irebe 'came'. bi keġekü büleġe is 'I was one who says', i.e. 'I would say' (Ming 我 (說)的 有來): the participle -kü + büleġe forms a past habitual or intended statement. So this is the cover story he meant to tell the enemy.

morph.gloss: you (plural; oblique stem of ta) [您 行]
this much, so much (Ming 這些) [這些]
to hasten, press on (stem inferred; Ming 趕到) [趕到着]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: Nama-ji ünen bolγažu qubčasun na-da ögčü asaraqu büleġe.
sentences.l: Me (acc.) true making, clothes me-to giving, raising was.
sentences.i: They would believe me, give me clothes and take me up.
sentences.n: Nama-ji ünen bolγažu is 'me true making' (Ming 我行 眞實 做着): ünen 'true' + bol- with the causative -γa-: 'taking me as true', and so 'trusting me'. na-da is 'to me', dative. asaraqu is 'raising, fostering' (Ming 擡擧); with büleġe it again carries the 'was going to' sense. This is the second half of the plan: the enemy would receive him.

morph.gloss: me (oblique stem of bi "I") [我 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to raise up, care for (Ming 擡擧) [擡擧]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: Bi morin unuγ̇ad üžetele edüi žaγ̇ura ülü-ü irekü büleġe bi.
sentences.l: I horse mounting watching this-much meanwhile not-? coming was I.
sentences.i: I would have mounted a horse and come back in no time.
sentences.n: bi morin unuγ̇ad is 'I, a horse mounting'. üžetele is 'while watching' (Ming 敎看着), edüi žaγ̇ura 'this much between' (Ming 這些 間): a short interval. ülü-ü irekü büleġe bi, Ming 不 來的麽 有來 我, 'would I not have come?'. The sense I give is 'I would have been back before you had watched for long'. Doubtful: the Ming 敎看着 'making look' may point to a different reading.

morph.gloss: this much, so much (Ming 這些) [這些]
question particle (Ming 麽 on the next word)
past: there was, used to be

sentences.t: Tein sedkižü qaγ̇an-u qaṅqaγsan sedkil elüssügei keġen
sentences.l: Thus thinking Qaγan's parched heart 'let-it-be-reached' saying,
sentences.i: Thinking so, 'Let me soothe the parched heart of the Qahan,'
sentences.n: tein sedkižü is 'thus thinking' (Ming 那般 想着). qaγ̇an-u qaṅqaγsan sedkil is 'the Qahan's heart that has dried up' (Ming 皇帝的 枯渴了的 心). elüssügei (Ming 趕上) carries an optative ending -sügei, 'may it, let it', and the stem is only the Ming's 'catch up with'; I read 'let it be reached, relieved'.

morph.gloss: to be parched, dried up (Ming 枯渴) [枯渴了的]
to reach, catch up with (stem uncertain; Ming 趕上) [趕上]

sentences.t: nidün qara ein sedkižü oduluγ̇a bi" keġebe.
sentences.l: Eyes black thus thinking went I," said.
sentences.i: with my eyes dark, I went." So he said.
sentences.n: nidün qara is 'eye black' (Ming 眼 黑): I take it as 'blindly, regardless', since the Qahan uses the same phrase of Jelme in his reply. ein is 'thus' (Ming 這般), sedkižü 'thinking'; oduluγ̇a is 'went' (Ming 去了來) with -luγ̇a the past. bi" closes the quotation; keġebe is outside.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün: "Edoġe jaγ̇un keġekü.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan saying: "Now what to-say.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said: "What more is there to say now?
sentences.n: Edoġe 'now' (Ming 如今) and jaγ̇un keġekü 'what is to be said' (Ming 甚麽 說): a rhetorical question, 'what is there to say'. keġekü is the participle in -kü. The quotation continues in the following units.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.t: Erte üdür γurban Merkid iležü Burqan-(n)i γurbanta qučiγ̇ulqui-dur
sentences.l: Earlier day three Merkid going, Burqan (acc.) three-times circling-making-at-time
sentences.i: Once, when the three Merkid came and made me circle Burqan three times,
sentences.n: Erte üdür 'formerly, in the earlier day' (Ming 在前 日子); γurban Merkid is 'three Merkid'. iležü 'going' is from ile-; the Ming 去着 says 'go', though elsewhere this verb has been doubtful for me. Burqan-(n)i is the accusative of the mountain name. qučiγ̇ulqui-dur is quči- 'go round' (stem inferred) + causative -γ̇ul- + participle -qui + -dur, 'at the time of making go round' (Ming 敎繞 時).

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people (people name) [種名]
to go (Ming 去; the verb is doubtful elsewhere) [去着]
Burqan, the holy mountain (mountain name) [山名 行]
accusative: marks the object (the bracketed n is Shiratori's)
to go round (stem inferred; Ming 繞) [敎繞 時]

sentences.t: amin min-u nigente abču γaruluγ̇a či.
sentences.l: my life once taking, brought-out you.
sentences.i: you took my life in your hand at once and brought me out.
sentences.n: amin min-u is 'life of mine' (Ming 性命 我的). nigente is Ming 一次, 'once' (the ending -te as 'times' is my guess). abču is 'taking' (ab- + -ču). γaruluγ̇a is the causative of γar- 'go out' with -uγ̇a, 'brought out' (Ming 出了來).

morph.gloss: once, one time (Ming 一次) [一次]

sentences.t: Edöġe basa qaγču büküi čisun-i ama-γ̇ar šimižü
sentences.l: Now again dry being blood (acc.) mouth-with sucking,
sentences.i: Now again you have sucked the dry blood into your mouth,
sentences.n: Edöġe 'now', basa 'again'. qaγču büküi is 'dry being' (Ming 乾着 有的), a participle of bü- 'be' after the converb. čisun-i is accusative; ama-γ̇ar 'with the mouth'; šimižü 'sucking'. This is one chain with the next unit.

morph.gloss: dry, having dried (converb; stem uncertain; Ming 乾着) [乾着]

sentences.t: amin min-u seṅtelbe či.
sentences.l: my life you opened.
sentences.i: and opened up my life again.
sentences.n: seṅtelbe is the Ming's 開豁了, 'opened up, cleared'; the stem seṅtel- is only the Ming's, and the sense is 'you brought me back to life'.

morph.gloss: to open up, clear (stem inferred; Ming 開豁) [開豁了]

sentences.t: Basa qaṅqažu amdurin büküi-dür amin-(n)i-jan örežü
sentences.l: Again parched, flustered being-when, life-own abandoning,
sentences.i: Again, when I was parched and bewildered, you cast aside your own life
sentences.n: Basa 'again'. qaṅqažu 'parched' (Ming 枯渴着), amdurin 'flustered', büküi-dür 'at the time of being' (Ming 有 時). amin-(n)i-jan is 'life' with -(n)i (a third-person possessive; the n is Shiratori's) and the reflexive -jan: 'your own life'. örežü is 'abandoning, throwing aside' (Ming 捨着).

morph.gloss: his, your (third-person possessive; the bracketed n is Shiratori's)
to cast aside, abandon (stem inferred; Ming 捨) [捨着]

sentences.t: daisun küġün-dür nidün qara orožu
sentences.l: Enemy people-to eyes black entering,
sentences.i: and went among the enemy with your eyes dark,
sentences.n: daisun 'hostile, enemy' (Ming 敵) with küġün-dür 'to people' (Ming 人行). nidün qara orožu, 'eyes black entering': the same idiom as Jelme's, here said by the Qahan, 'blindly, heedlessly'.

sentences.t: undan qaṅγažü amin min-u oroγ̇ulba či.
sentences.l: Drink satisfying, life my caused-to-enter you.
sentences.i: and with a drink you restored my life.
sentences.n: undan is 'drink' (Ming 飮), qaṅγažü 'satisfying' (Ming 足着). amin min-u oroγ̇ulba is 'life of mine you made enter', the causative of oro- 'enter', i.e. 'put life back into me'. či closes the sentence.

sentences.t: Ede γurban tusas-i čin-u sedkil dotora min-u atuγai keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: These three favours (acc.) your heart inside my let-them-remain saying, decree made.
sentences.i: 'These three favours of yours I shall keep within my heart,' he decreed.
sentences.n: Ede 'these' and γurban 'three' (Ming 這的每 三件); tusas-i is tusa 'favour' (Ming 恩) + plural -s + accusative. čin-u sedkil dotora min-u atuγai is hard: the Ming reads 你的 心 內 我的 存着, 'your heart inside my let-remain', and I take it as 'let them remain within my heart', with čin-u 'your' going with the favours, not the heart. atuγai is the Ming's 存着 and a hortative ending -γai. keġen 'saying' and žarliγ bolba 'a decree was made' (Ming 聖旨 做了): Chinggis pronounces his thanks as an order.

morph.gloss: inside, within (here "in me", Ming 內行) [內]
let it remain, let it be kept (Ming 存着; hortative -γai on an uncertain stem) [存着]
